name: Deliberate orthographic manipulation for double meaning
instruction: Score 0-10 for whether a spelling change, homophone swap, or unusual word choice is clearly deliberate and produces an added layer of meaning. A 10 is a clearly intentional alteration that adds a pun or ambiguity. A 0 is standard spelling throughout, or an error that adds no meaning.

name: Layered wordplay
instruction: Score 10 when the wording supports two simultaneous meanings that reinforce each other; score 0 when it has only one literal reading.

name: Self-contained readability
instruction: Score 10 when the joke is fully understandable from the text alone without external media or missing context; score 0 when it requires a link, image, or substantial reconstruction.

name: Extent of capitalised or shouted typography
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of the text is set in capital letters or otherwise typographically shouted (ALL-CAPS words, repeated letters, strings of exclamation marks). 10 = the text is dominated by shouted typography; 0 = ordinary sentence case throughout. Count the typography only; do not judge whether it is good or whether the item is funny.

name: Inventiveness of title-substitution (vs. rote swap)
instruction: Score 0-10 how inventive a movie/show-title-based joke is. A 10 reworks the source title with a surprising, multi-layered mapping onto the new topic. A 0 is a single rote word-swap into an otherwise-unchanged famous title with minimal added wit.

name: Trailing furniture: hashtags, handles, parenthetical byline
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much non-sentence furniture is appended at the end of the text -- trailing hashtags, @-handles, a parenthetical name and town, or similar tags. 10 = several such tags appended; 0 = the text ends with the sentence itself. Count the furniture only; this is not a judgement of writing quality.

name: Capitalised words, tag count and overall length
instruction: This is a counting task, not a quality judgement. Estimate three quantities from the item as typed: (a) how many words begin with a capital letter or are fully capitalised, expressed as a share of all words, and the resulting share of uppercase letters overall, (b) the number of @handles and #hashtags, (c) the total character count. Convert to one 0-10 extent number, weighting (a) most heavily, then (b), then (c). Score 0 when the item is entirely lower case with no handles or hashtags beyond the contest prompt tag and is short. Score 5 when a minority of words are capitalised, as in a single title rendered in title case inside an otherwise plain sentence, or one handle or hashtag appears, or the item is of middling length. Score 10 when most words carry capitals or whole runs are in block capitals, three or more handles and hashtags appear, and the item is long. Count only. Do NOT decide whether the capitalisation is warranted, correct, stylish or lazy, and do NOT let the inventiveness or dullness of the wording change the number.

name: Meta-reference to the show/submission process itself
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much the tweet's content is about the act of being on the show, tweeting, or the contest mechanics itself (rather than about the assigned topic), where 0 = no such meta-reference and 10 = the tweet is entirely about the submission process/show. Score only presence of this meta-content -- do NOT judge whether it is clever.

name: Reference recontextualization
instruction: Score 10 when a movie, celebrity, or cultural reference is altered to make a sharp comment about the prompt; score 0 when a reference is pasted in with only superficial substitution.

name: Vivid Scene Specificity
instruction: Score the immediacy and specificity of the mental scene: 10 means the text instantly depicts a distinctive comic situation, while 0 means it remains abstract, generic, or image-poor.

name: Promotion and link residue
instruction: Rate 0-10 for how much the tweet contains outward-promotion or attachment residue, such as URLs, extra promotional hashtags, or media-directed wording. Judge only visible text; do not judge whether this feature is good, funny, or desirable.

name: Vernacular spelling
instruction: Rate 0-10 for how much the wording uses regionally marked vernacular, eye-dialect, or nonstandard contractions and spellings. Judge only visible text; do not judge whether this feature is good, funny, or desirable.

name: Phonetic snap
instruction: Score 10 when rhythm, stress, repetition, or sound pattern makes the line naturally satisfying to say; score 0 when its phrasing is awkward or sonically flat.

name: Altered title implies a developed new work
instruction: Read the item beside its contest prompt and locate the recognisable title, name or catchphrase being altered. Score 10 when the alteration forces a coherent new work or scenario into view and the item does at least some of the work of showing it: the changed element has a consequence, so a reader can infer a different plot, a different protagonist, a different genre or a different stakes structure, and the original title's shape still holds the new content together. Score 5 when the alteration implies something new but nothing beyond the swapped element is developed, so the reader must supply the entire idea. Score 0 when only a word or syllable has been exchanged for a similar-sounding or same-category word and nothing about the imagined work changes, including pure spelling play, pluralisation and one-letter swaps. Judge the transformation only. Do NOT let length, capitalisation, title case, punctuation, quotation marks, emoji, @handles or #hashtags move the number: a short, all-lowercase, untagged item may score 10, and a long item in emphatic capitals with several tags may score 0. Capitalised title case is a convention of writing titles and is not evidence of depth.

name: Implied Narrative
instruction: Score how much the wording implies a funny before-and-after sequence or escalating event: 10 means a tiny line suggests a whole story, while 0 means it is only a static label or list.

name: Sheer text bulk, with shouting and tags counted
instruction: This is a measurement task, not a quality judgement. Estimate three quantities from the item as typed: (a) its total character count, (b) the share of alphabetic characters that are uppercase, (c) the number of @handles and #hashtags. Convert to one 0-10 extent number, weighting (a) most heavily, then (b), then (c). Score 0 for a very short item, roughly under forty characters, in plain lower or sentence case with no handles or hashtags beyond the contest prompt tag. Score 5 for an item of middling length, roughly a third to two thirds of the platform limit, with occasional capitalised words or a single handle or hashtag. Score 10 for an item running to the platform limit or close to it, especially when combined with heavy uppercase or three or more handles and hashtags. Count what is on the page. Do NOT decide whether the item is funny, crude, clever, tasteless or well made, and do NOT let the content shift the number: two items of identical length and typography receive identical scores regardless of what they say.

name: Off-contest hashtag stuffing and points solicitation
instruction: Score the EXTENT of hashtags beyond the single contest hashtag. 10 = two or more additional hashtags unrelated to answering the prompt, including tags that solicit attention from the show or attach the entry to a separate trend. 5 = exactly one extra hashtag. 0 = the contest hashtag only. Count tags; do NOT judge whether the extra tags are witty, well chosen, annoying, or spammy, and do not let the joke's quality influence the count.

name: Semantic economy
instruction: Score 10 when nearly every content word adds distinct comic information; score 0 when the joke contains padding, repetition, or arbitrary wording.

name: Rushed-editing residue
instruction: Rate 0-10 for how much the wording shows rushed-editing residue, including agreement errors, typos, malformed syntax, or visible correction attempts. Judge only visible text; do not judge whether this feature is good, funny, or desirable.

name: Hashtag capitalization style (camelCase vs lowercase)
instruction: Score 0-10 for how consistently the contest hashtag is written in CamelCase (each word capitalized) versus all-lowercase or irregular casing, where 0 = fully lowercase/irregular and 10 = fully and consistently CamelCased. Score only the typographic pattern -- do NOT judge whether this makes the tweet better.

name: Uppercase share plus tag and handle furniture
instruction: This is a counting task, not a quality judgement. Estimate three quantities from the item text as typed: (a) the share of alphabetic characters that are uppercase, (b) the number of @handles and #hashtags present, (c) the overall character length. Convert to one 0-10 extent number, weighting (a) most heavily, then (b), then (c). Score 0 when the item is entirely lower case or plain sentence case, contains no @handle and no #hashtag beyond the contest prompt tag itself, and is short. Score 5 when roughly a tenth to a fifth of letters are uppercase, or one or two handles/hashtags appear, or the item runs to moderate length. Score 10 when a third or more of the letters are uppercase (including any fully capitalised word runs), three or more @handles/#hashtags appear, and the item runs near the maximum length. Do NOT decide whether any of this is good, funny, appropriate, lazy or skilled, and do NOT let the wit, cleverness or dullness of the content raise or lower the number. A brilliant line and a worthless line typed identically must receive the same score.

name: Premise that only this prompt could support
instruction: Read the item beside the contest prompt it was written for. Judge one thing: does the item supply a specific premise that reinterprets the prompt, or does it merely name something the prompt already implies? Score 10 when the item commits to a particular situation, voice or logic that is locked to this prompt: swap in a different prompt of the same shape and the line would stop making sense. Score 5 when a real reinterpretation is present but loose enough that several unrelated prompts could host the same line unchanged. Score 0 when the item is a literal restatement of the prompt, a dictionary-style association, or a stock phrase with the prompt's words dropped in. Judge the idea only. Do NOT let length, capitalisation, punctuation, emoji, @handles or #hashtags move the number in either direction: a six-word, all-lowercase, untagged line with a tightly fitting premise must be able to score 10, and a maximum-length, ALL-CAPS, three-hashtag line whose content is a generic association must be able to score 0. If you find yourself crediting effort, volume or emphasis rather than fit of premise, lower the score.

name: Specific Satirical Target
instruction: Score the precision of the target: 10 means the line points at a concrete person, institution, behavior, or practice with a compressed angle, while 0 means it expresses only a vague attitude or slogan.

name: Concrete topical mechanism
instruction: Score 10 when the hashtag topic is connected to a concrete behavior, contradiction, or institution; score 0 when the line merely includes topical keywords or labels.

name: A specific concrete detail carries the joke
instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the comic work is done by a specific, concrete particular (a named thing, an exact number, a precise action) rather than by a generic category word. 10 = one vivid particular is doing the work; 0 = only generic labels, nothing specific enough to picture. Judge the specificity of the comic content, not the length.

name: Sets up an expectation and then turns it
instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the wording first leads the reader toward one reading and then supplies a different one. 10 = a clear setup and a clear turn away from it; 0 = a single flat statement with no setup and nothing turned. Judge the comic structure, not the typography.

name: Mechanism survives removing the crudest element
instruction: Identify the single most taboo, gross, obscene or shocking word or image in the item. Mentally replace it with a neutral placeholder of the same grammatical role, then re-read the item against its contest prompt. Score 10 when the line still works after the substitution because the machinery is elsewhere: a misdirection, an unexpected but exact category error, a precise observation, an implied character, a structural reversal. Score 5 when something survives but is thin, so the substituted version reads as a mild version of the same idea rather than a working line. Score 0 when the placeholder version has nothing left at all, that is, when the transgressive term was the whole event and the surrounding words were only setup for it. Judge only what survives the substitution. Do NOT let length, capitalisation, punctuation, emoji, @handles or #hashtags move the number: a short, plainly typed, untagged item whose mechanism survives must be able to score 10, and a long, fully capitalised, handle-stuffed item that collapses to nothing without its obscenity must be able to score 0. Do not reward or penalise the presence of the crude term itself; judge only what is left when it is gone.

name: Ordinal or sequel escalation over an already-obvious source
instruction: MODE 3, position fingerprint. Score the EXTENT to which the text reads as a bid placed on top of a source someone else would obviously have claimed first: a number bumped one step past the canonical title, a sequel number, a colon-appended follow-on, or a 'part two' framing of a reference whose plain form is the first thing anyone would reach for. 10 = the entry only makes sense as an escalation of an already-taken obvious take. 5 = a familiar source used with a modest twist. 0 = no escalation structure; the source is either fresh or used plainly. You cannot see the entry's actual position in the stream -- score only the textual tell. Do NOT judge whether escalating was a good move.

name: Implicit scene completion
instruction: Score 10 when a short line makes the reader instantly imagine a specific comic scene or preceding event; score 0 when it supplies no actionable situation beyond a fragment.
